old: I wanted to blow him up too
new: I wanted to give him a piece of my mind too
reason: "Blow him up" is heard as "explode him"; the meaning is to scold him.

old: the United States of America, as we used to call them in school
new: the United States of America, as we used to call trousers in school
reason: A listener cannot tell that the school joke name refers to the trousers he is about to show.

old: in the corner by the door, I stepped on a box
new: in the corner behind the door, I stepped on a box
reason: Raskolnikov immediately echoes "Behind the door?" and Razumihin later says the murderer stood behind the door, so the spot should be named the same way here.

old: in the empty apartment while Nikolay and Dmitri had just run out
new: in the empty apartment, which Nikolay and Dmitri had just run out of
reason: "While ... had just run out" is tense-tangled and hard to parse on first hearing.

old: Razumihin continued, whose easy familiarity seemed
new: Razumihin continued. His easy familiarity seemed
reason: The relative clause "whose" hangs off the verb instead of a noun, which is ungrammatical.

old: His dark mutton-chop whiskers framed both sides nicely, growing thick on his shining, clean-shaven chin.
new: His dark mutton-chop whiskers grew thick on both cheeks, nicely framing his shining, clean-shaven chin.
reason: Whiskers "growing thick on" a "clean-shaven chin" sounds self-contradictory.

old: And then the great moment came, and
new: And then the great moment came[*], and
reason: The translator's note in the next paragraph has no matching [*] marker, so the reader cannot tell which phrase it explains.
